subject: ZephyrBI renewal — proposal for price-match, credit bridge, and capacity increase
messages:
From: Rajiv Singh <rajiv.singh@zephyrbi.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Cc: maya.rao@zephyrbi.com
Date: 2027-02-18T08:45:00-08:00
Subject: Renewal pricing + capacity bump discussion

Hi Stephanie,

We’re coming up on our annual renewal and seeing sustained growth across two of our product lines — we expect token consumption to be ~2.6x what we committed to this year. We’d like to discuss options for a 12–18 month renewal that:
- Adds a permanent capacity uplift (approx +70% peak throughput)
- Keeps per-token economics stable (we’ve seen price movement from several providers)
- Includes a short-term bridge while we finalize budget (1–3 months)

Can you share available options and availability for a quick call this week? Maya and I are available Wed/Thu after 11am PT.

Thanks,
Rajiv
VP Product, ZephyrBI
[Attachment: Usage_Stats_FY2026_Q4.csv (CSV)]

From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
To: Rajiv Singh <rajiv.singh@zephyrbi.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: 2027-02-18T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal pricing + capacity bump discussion

Hi Rajiv — thanks for the note and congrats on the growth.

Quick availability: Thu 2/19 11:30am PT works for me — I’ve penciled it in.

High-level, we can do a couple of conservative paths:
1) 12-month renewal with a 70% committed capacity increase + 90-day price-match (we’ll hold current rates for the first 3 months while your procurement signs off).
2) 18-month renewal with a tiered commit and a one-time onboarding credit (applied to first invoice) — this gets you a deeper unit discount.
3) Short-term bridge: one-off consumption credits to cover overage for the next 30–60 days while we finalize the new commit.

I’ll bring Marcus (pricing) to the call; he can run the economics. Can you confirm which documents you want attached (SOW, usage breakdown)?

—Stephanie
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: none yet]

From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
To: marcus_lin@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2027-02-18T11:12:00-08:00
Subject: ZephyrBI renewal — prep and recommended structure (internal)

Folks — quick prep for the Thu 11:30am PT call with ZephyrBI. They’re at ~2.6x committed consumption and asking for a +70% committed capacity.

My recommended structure:
- Offer A (12m): 70% committed uplift; price-match for months 1–3 (no change to existing unit rates during that window); one-time $30k onboarding credit to offset migration/config.
- Offer B (18m): 70% uplift with tiered unit discounts starting month 4; no price-match period but larger committed discount.
- Bridge: If procurement needs time, provide a 60-day consumption credit capped at $40k.

We should include a clause: if average monthly consumption over first 90 days exceeds committed level by >25%, auto-escalation to the next tier (to protect capacity). Also, propose manual invoice schedule: monthly rather than net-30 to align cash flows for Zephyr.

Marcus — can you run numbers on Offer A vs Offer B (unit economics + margin impact) before 3pm today? Rishi — any red flags on the auto-escalation wording from a product/ops standpoint? Lauren — I may need a one-time exec approval for the price-match window if we go with Offer A.

Thanks,
Stephanie

From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
To: Rajiv Singh <rajiv.singh@zephyrbi.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2027-02-19T12:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal pricing + capacity bump discussion

Rajiv — great to meet earlier. Per our call, here’s a written proposal to review with procurement: 

Proposal (summary):
- Term: 12 months starting on signature date
- Committed capacity: +70% peak throughput (details in attached SOW)
- Price: current unit rates honored for first 90 days (price-match window). From month 4, rates revert to committed-tier pricing in SOW.
- One-time onboarding credit: $30,000 applied to first invoice
- Bridge protection: up to $40,000 in consumption credits for the first 60 days if procurement timing delays signature
- Invoicing: Monthly invoices; Zephyr prefers net-30 — willing to align if accounting signs off
- Ops safeguard: auto-escalation clause if actuals exceed committed baseline by >25% for 90-day rolling average — this routes to capacity ops and pricing review

Attached: Zephyr_Renewal_SOW_v3.pdf (SOW with commit numbers and SLAs) and Usage_Stats_FY2026_Q4.csv (you already shared).

Next steps: If this looks good, I’ll issue an updated SOW and DocuSign envelope for signatures. If procurement wants a different invoicing cadence, loop in billing and we’ll adjust.

—Stephanie
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Zephyr_Renewal_SOW_v3.pdf (PDF); Usage_Stats_FY2026_Q4.csv (CSV)]

From: Rajiv Singh <rajiv.singh@zephyrbi.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Cc: accounts@zephyrbi.com
Date: 2027-02-22T10:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal pricing + capacity bump discussion

Stephanie — thanks for the clear proposal. Procurement is generally happy with the structure. A couple of asks before we sign: 
1) Can the price-match window be extended to 120 days? Procurement prefers a slightly longer buffer while our Q2 budgets are finalized.
2) We prefer invoicing on a net-45 cadence this cycle — can Redwood accommodate that for Zephyr?

If you can confirm those two items I’ll get our billing team to expect the DocuSign and circulate for signatures.

Thanks,
Rajiv

From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
To: Rajiv Singh <rajiv.singh@zephyrbi.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: 2027-02-24T15:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal pricing + capacity bump discussion

Rajiv — appreciate the quick review. We can accommodate both asks with one condition: extend the price-match window to 120 days and accept a small phased billing holdback that protects Redwood if usage spikes beyond the agreed committed level in the first 60 days. Details: 

- Price-match window: 120 days
- Invoicing: net-45 OK for this renewal (billing to accounts@zephyrbi.com)
- Holdback: 10% of first two invoices retained for 45 days and applied to any overage that exceeds committed baseline >25% during first 60 days. If no overage, holdback released and credit applied to month 3 invoice.

I’m prepping the DocuSign now — you should see an envelope within 2 hours. DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.com/ZephyrBI-Renewal-ZF-2027

If that’s acceptable, I’ll route to legal to lock the small contract amendment language for the holdback.

—Stephanie
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: none]
